overview_raw: Note: This program has replaced the Fire Executive Management Industry Partnership Certificate. Please visit the Entrance Requirements page to apply. Delivery: blended. See details . Lead with confidence in the moments that matter—from the fire hall to the council chamber. The Certificate in Fire Service Industry Leadership helps experienced firefighters and officers strengthen the leadership skills required to guide teams, make sound decisions under pressure, and represent their department with credibility in a complex, public environment. Through a cohort-based learning experience—delivered primarily in person at fire halls and supported by online coursework—participants build practical capability in communication, labour relations, municipal finance and governance, change leadership, and inclusive people practices. Learning is applied immediately to real operational challenges, helping participants prepare to step into exempt officer roles and other senior leadership positions with a clear leadership approach and a stronger organizational lens. With cohorts drawn from across the BC Fire Service and sessions hosted in fire halls, the program supports a province-wide perspective on emerging issues and practices while building relationships that strengthen collaboration beyond participants’ home departments. About the program 32 credits total (16 1-credit courses and two 8-credit capstone projects). Organized into four microcredentials, each stackable and independently recognizable. Cohort-based delivery scheduled in partnership with fire departments. Predominantly in-person: face-to-face courses at fire halls with some online coursework. Graduates are eligible to apply for the Executive Pathway into BCIT’s Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) program. Who it’s for Structured as a series of stackable microcredentials, this program is accessible to both exempt officers and union members at various stages of their careers. Industry partnership Built on extensive consultation with Fire Chiefs, Deputy Fire Chiefs, Assistant Fire Chiefs, and union representatives from across the province, the program delivers contextually relevant, applied leadership education designed specifically for the Fire Service Industry. entrance_requirements_raw: Application processing Applications are accepted throughout the year. Applications are submitted by prospective students upon approval by their sponsoring organizations. Speak with your Fire Chief to begin the sponsorship process. Entrance requirements Applicants must meet the following entrance requirements: English language proficiency: Category 2 – English Studies 12 (67%) or equivalent Approval from Fire Chief/Department to enrol International applicants This program is not available to international students. View available programs . Apply to program Applications for this program are processed by the SoBM Business Administration Department. Once a student has approval to enrol in the program, please reach out to BCIT_firstresponder@bcit.ca to begin the application process. For more information, please contact Thomas Turniawan . completion_requirements_raw: After completing the prescribed course work, all degree program students are required to complete an industry-sponsored project in their selected area.
program_details_raw: Program delivery Blended: This program is delivered partly on campus and partly online. The program is delivered in cohorts, scheduled in coordination with fire departments. Scheduling options include weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly session formats, determined in partnership with the participating departments. Program structure The Certificate in Fire Service Industry Leadership is organized around four interconnected microcredentials and two capstone projects. The microcredentials each consist of four 1-credit courses delivered in a blended format—face-to-face workshop sessions held at fire halls across the region, combined with online learning. Microcredential 1: Leadership Foundations — Self, Teams, & Collective Performance Leadership development is the bridge between strong, operational experience and the next stage of responsibility—supervising people, improving performance, and shaping how the work gets done. Grounded in leadership foundations across self, team, and collective performance, participants strengthen self-awareness and decision-making, practice tools that build alignment and accountability, and develop practical approaches to improve productivity by matching people, roles, and resources. The courses in this microcredential support immediate application, while preparing participants to take on greater supervisory and leadership responsibility. Microcredential 2: Leading an Engaged & Inclusive Organization Engagement and inclusion don’t happen by accident. They are built through everyday leadership practices that help people feel they belong, can contribute, and are supported to perform at their best. Participants develop practical skills to strengthen equity and inclusion, communicate with clarity and care in difficult conversations, and connect day-to-day decisions to organizational purpose and culture. Microcredential 3: Leading Change — Influence & Impact Change succeeds when people understand the “why,” trust the process, and see their role in making it real. Focused on influence and impact, this microcredential strengthens the skills leaders need to move from identifying complex problems to mobilizing stakeholders and sustaining adoption. Participants build confidence in creative problem solving, practice communication approaches that connect and persuade, and apply change-management tools to plan, lead, measure, and reinforce meaningful change in their teams and organizations. Microcredential 4: Leading in a Municipal Environment In municipal environments, leadership is exercised as much through policy, budgets, and relationships as it is through operations. Grounded in the realities of local government, this microcredential helps participants navigate the systems that shape municipal organizations—labour relations and collective agreements, financial stewardship and procurement, fair and effective recruitment and onboarding, and the governance structures that influence decisions and accountability. Participants leave better equipped to represent their organization with credibility, make informed recommendations, and lead with confidence within the broader public-service context. Capstone Projects: Two work-integrated learning projects, with in-person kickoff sessions, scheduled faculty check-ins, and a final written report and presentation delivered to department leadership. Continue your education Graduates of this certificate are eligible to apply for admission into BCIT's Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) program through the existing Executive Pathway . An Experience-Based Placement assessment will determine bridging requirements for admission. Go back Courses Next up Contact Us

courses.course_name: Lead From Within: Sharpen Your Edge
courses.component_name: Microcredential 1 – Leadership Foundations: Self, Teams, & Collective Performance
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​​Leadership begins with understanding yourself. This course focuses on developing self-awareness as the foundation for effective leadership. Participants will explore how perceptions, assumptions, and biases shape their leadership style and identify personal strengths and challenges. Through reflection and planning, participants will create actionable strategies to foster growth and realize their leadership potential in today's evolving workplace.​​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.component_name: Microcredential 1 – Leadership Foundations: Self, Teams, & Collective Performance
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Leading teams in today's dynamic workplace requires a diverse set of skills to unlock the potential of people and resources. Building on the personal leadership style and strengths developed in Leadership 1: Self as Leader, participants will learn to apply these skills in team settings. This course introduces practical tools such as Team Charters and techniques like constructive feedback to foster collaboration, build trust, and enhance team performance.​ Prerequisite(s): S in XLED 1012

courses.component_name: Microcredential 1 – Leadership Foundations: Self, Teams, & Collective Performance
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​People thrive when they understand how their work contributes to the organization's purpose in a meaningful way. Effective supervisors align people, tasks, and resources to maximize productivity. This course provides practical strategies for defining the role of a supervisor, identifying tasks for delegation, and applying structured approaches to problem-solving and decision-making. By implementing consistent processes and practices, supervisors can create clarity, predictability, and a motivating environment that drives team performance.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Project Management: From Idea to Outcome 1
courses.component_name: Microcredential 1 – Leadership Foundations: Self, Teams, & Collective Performance
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Project management is a critical skill for achieving organizational goals and implementing change effectively. This course provides an overview of project management principles and introduces practical tools and techniques that can be applied to projects of any size. Participants will learn how to structure work, manage constraints, and apply proven methodologies to deliver successful outcomes. Designed for teams and professionals, this course emphasizes real-world application to improve efficiency and collaboration.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​As organizations increasingly recognize the critical role of DEI in fostering innovation, improving employee engagement, and enhancing overall performance, this course addresses the pressing need for leaders to champion these principles. By cultivating a deeper understanding of DEI, participants will be better prepared to create inclusive workplaces that attract and retain diverse talent, drive collaboration, and ultimately contribute to long-term organizational success. This course provides a comprehensive exploration of DEI principles and application, empowering leaders to effect meaningful change within their organizations.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.component_name: Microcredential 2 – Leading an Engaged & Inclusive Organization
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course equips participants with the skills and confidence to navigate challenging conversations in the workplace. Through practical strategies and interactive exercises, learners will explore techniques for managing emotions, fostering mutual understanding, and achieving constructive outcomes. The course emphasizes preparation, active listening, empathy, and problem-solving to transform difficult conversations into opportunities for collaboration and growth.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.component_name: Microcredential 2 – Leading an Engaged & Inclusive Organization
courses.prerequisite_raw: S in XLED 1012 and S in XLED 1022
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Building on the foundations of XLED 1012 and XLED 1022, this advanced course focuses on developing organizational leadership competencies. Participants will explore strategic planning and implementation, communication strategies, organizational performance measurement, and leading change. Through interactive activities, case studies, and experiential learning, participants will deepen their understanding of organizational culture, sub-cultures, and the responsibilities of being part of a leadership team. The course emphasizes accountability, adaptability, and the ability to align people and processes to achieve organizational goals.​ Prerequisite(s): S in XLED 1012 and S in XLED 1022

courses.course_name: Project Management: From Idea to Outcome 2
courses.component_name: Microcredential 2 – Leading an Engaged & Inclusive Organization
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course equips students with essential project management skills to ensure successful project delivery and maximize benefits realization. Participants will explore the critical factors that influence project success and failure and learn how to apply proven tools and techniques to mitigate risks and manage change effectively. By the end of the course, participants will have the practical knowledge and tools to plan, execute, and close projects effectively, ensuring value delivery and organizational success.​ Prerequisite(s): S in XOPM 1011

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Communication requires several skills. Effective communication requires individuals to skillfully navigate the application of those skills considering the topic, environmental factors and outcome requirements. Honing communication skills is paramount to enable individuals to learn and continue working together productively. Participants will learn and practice a wide variety of skills that drive effective interpersonal communication. ​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Creative Problem Solving: Insight to Impact
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Creative problem solving is a critical skill for navigating complex challenges in today's dynamic workplace. This course introduces participants to problem-solving methodologies that help identify root causes, generate innovative ideas, and implement effective solutions. Through interactive exercises and real-world applications, learners will practice structured approaches such as brainstorming, evaluation techniques, and decision-making frameworks to enhance their ability to solve problems creatively and collaboratively.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces the essential principles and practices of change management. Participants will explore the nature of organizational change, reflect on personal experiences, and learn how to define their role in driving successful transitions. Through interactive workshops, they will gain the foundational knowledge and confidence needed to lead change from any position—whether as a project lead, manager, or contributor.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.course_name: Leading Change: From Plan to Impact
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Building on concepts from XLED 1141, this course equips participants with advanced tools and strategies to map, implement, and sustain change. Learners will develop actionable plans, manage resistance, measure progress, and ensure long-term success.​ Prerequisite(s): S in XLED 1141

courses.component_name: Microcredential 4 – Leading in a Municipal Environment
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course provides a foundation in labour relations for municipal leaders moving into management positions. Participants will gain an understanding of the legal frameworks, collective agreements, and practical communication strategies that support effective union–management relationships within BC municipalities.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.component_name: Microcredential 4 – Leading in a Municipal Environment
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​Municipal leaders transitioning into management need to understand the financial and procurement frameworks that govern BC municipalities. This course provides a foundation in municipal budgeting, accounting principles, and procurement practices. Participants will develop the ability to read budgets, make informed spending decisions, and apply ethical procurement processes that ensure transparency and accountability.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.component_name: Microcredential 4 – Leading in a Municipal Environment
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course explores effective recruitment, selection, and onboarding practices for municipal leaders working within municipal and unionized environments. Participants will learn how to plan equitable and transparent hiring processes, develop competency-based selection tools, and design onboarding strategies that foster engagement and retention.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.component_name: Microcredential 4 – Leading in a Municipal Environment
courses.prerequisite_raw: No prerequisites are required for this course.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course introduces municipal leaders to the structures, systems, and processes of municipal governance in British Columbia. Participants will gain a comprehensive understanding of how local governments operate, make decisions, and interact with provincial authorities, with a focus on systems thinking and practical governance processes.​ Prerequisite(s): No prerequisites are required for this course.

courses.prerequisite_raw: S in XLED 1012 and S in XLED 1022 and S in XLED 1061 and S in XOPM 1011 and S in XOPM 2011 and S in XCOR 1201 and S in XLED 1052 and S in XLED 1111 or approval from the Program Head.
courses.course_overview_raw: ​This course is designed to empower students to apply the leadership and project management skills gained from the first two Microcredentials in a real-world team or departmental context. Students will complete an individual capstone project to diagnose organizational challenges or opportunities using proven leadership frameworks, design targeted interventions and develop actionable plans. They will select a focus area for their project—such as strategic planning, team culture development, productivity enhancement, or conflict resolution —and create professional artifacts alongside a comprehensive project plan.​ Prerequisite(s): S in XLED 1012 and S in XLED 1022 and S in XLED 1061 and S in XOPM 1011 and S in XOPM 2011 and S in XCOR 1201 and S in XLED 1052 and S in XLED 1111 or approval from the Program Head.

courses.prerequisite_raw: S in XLED 1012 and S in XLED 1022 and S in XLED 1061 and S in XOPM 1011 and S in XOPM 2011 and S in XCOR 1201 and S in XLED 1052 and S in XLED 1111 and 50% in CORP 2000 and S in XLED 1141 and S in XLED 2141 and S in XLED 1041 and S in XCOR 1031 and S in XLED 2001 and S in XLED 2011 and S in XLED 2031 and S in XLED 2021 or approval from the Program Head
courses.course_overview_raw: This capstone course provides participants with the opportunity to synthesize and apply the full range of knowledge and skills developed throughout the program to a complex, organization-wide leadership initiative. Participants will lead the design of a comprehensive operational excellence project that addresses systemic challenges and opportunities within their organization. Participants will assess current-state operations, identify strategic improvement opportunities, and propose evidence-based solutions that balance performance, compliance, equity, and sustainability. Participants may choose to focus their capstone project on one or more of the following areas: Inclusive operations Constructive labour relations Ethical and responsible financial management Equitable recruitment and onboarding practices Productivity and operational effectiveness at scale Participants will submit a final written report and deliver a presentation. The capstone is designed to prepare participants for senior or cross-functional roles requiring strategic oversight, change leadership, and measurable organizational impact.​ Prerequisite(s): S in XLED 1012 and S in XLED 1022 and S in XLED 1061 and S in XOPM 1011 and S in XOPM 2011 and S in XCOR 1201 and S in XLED 1052 and S in XLED 1111 and 50% in CORP 2000 and S in XLED 1141 and S in XLED 2141 and S in XLED 1041 and S in XCOR 1031 and S in XLED 2001 and S in XLED 2011 and S in XLED 2031 and S in XLED 2021 or approval from the Program Head
